sources.citation: Michael Meli, Matthew R. McNiece and Bradley Reaves (2019). How Bad Can It Git? Characterizing Secret Leakage in Public GitHub Repositories. NDSS.
sources.supports: Historical evidence of credential leakage in public GitHub repositories; motivates defensive scanning.
sources.limits: Does not measure today's leakage rate, private repositories or Veil Guard performance.

sources.citation: Jesse Burdick-Pless (2025). Beyond RegEx – Heuristic-based Secret Detection. MS thesis, Rochester Institute of Technology.
sources.supports: Related work on heuristic/vector and neural-network approaches to secret detection; advisor listed as Ivona Bezakova.
sources.limits: Not a KNN validation, not the source of our eight features; full thesis experiments have not been independently assessed.

sources.citation: Thomas M. Cover and Peter E. Hart (1967). Nearest Neighbor Pattern Classification. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 13(1), 21–27.
sources.reviewed: Original paper, introductory definitions and stated asymptotic result
sources.supports: Foundational nearest-neighbour classification.
sources.limits: Asymptotic results under assumptions do not guarantee finite-data accuracy for this project.

sources.citation: Cornell University CS4780 (2018). Lecture 2: k-nearest neighbors / Curse of Dimensionality.
sources.supports: KNN classification, distance choice and geometric limitations.
sources.limits: Illustrative teaching material; does not endorse eight dimensions or our application.

sources.citation: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe (2018). Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra: Vectors, Matrices, and Least Squares. Cambridge University Press.
sources.reviewed: Author-hosted book page and linked teaching resources
sources.supports: Background for vectors, norms, matrices and linear transformations.
sources.limits: Our eight-feature representation and worked example are project constructions.

sources.citation: Claude E. Shannon (1948). A Mathematical Theory of Communication. Bell System Technical Journal 27, 379–423 and 623–656.
sources.supports: Mathematical background for discrete Shannon entropy.
sources.limits: Character-frequency entropy of one string is not a measure of credential validity or a password-strength guarantee.

sources.citation: Robert A. Wagner and Michael J. Fischer (1974). The String-to-String Correction Problem. Journal of the ACM 21(1), 168–173.
sources.reviewed: Original article, abstract and edit-distance definition
sources.supports: Insertion, deletion and substitution edit distance.
sources.limits: The normalised placeholder similarity and dictionary are our choices, not a proven security classifier.

sources.citation: Kilian Q. Weinberger and Lawrence K. Saul (2009). Distance Metric Learning for Large Margin Nearest Neighbor Classification. JMLR 10, 207–244.
sources.reviewed: Journal abstract and author publication record
sources.supports: Related work on learned distance metrics and linear transformations before nearest-neighbour classification.
sources.limits: Veil Guard v1 uses fixed standardisation and Euclidean distance; it does not implement LMNN.

sources.citation: Kilian Quirin Weinberger (2007). Metric Learning with Convex Optimization. PhD dissertation, University of Pennsylvania; supervisor Lawrence K. Saul.
sources.reviewed: Title-page metadata and author's publication listing; full dissertation not reviewed
sources.supports: Further academic reading on metric learning; bibliographic details corroborated by the author.
sources.limits: Background reading only; no implementation or performance claim relies on unreviewed chapters.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. StandardScaler API documentation.
sources.supports: Train-fitted centring/scaling, ddof=0 and scale 1 for zero variance.
sources.limits: Standardisation does not guarantee better detection or remove feature correlation.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. Common pitfalls and recommended practices.
sources.supports: Separate training/test data and fit preprocessing only on training data.
sources.limits: Our connected-family split design is a project adaptation, not a claim that a library discovers leakage automatically.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. GroupKFold API documentation.
sources.supports: Cross-validation with group-disjoint folds.
sources.limits: We must construct correct groups and verify them; GroupKFold alone cannot identify related fixtures.

sources.citation: Takaya Saito and Marc Rehmsmeier (2015). The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets. PLOS ONE 10(3), e0118432.
sources.supports: Rationale for precision/recall-based assessment under class imbalance.
sources.limits: Does not prescribe our Precision@20, acceptance threshold or bootstrap protocol.

sources.citation: Sayash Kapoor and Arvind Narayanan (2023). Leakage and the reproducibility crisis in machine-learning-based science. Patterns 4(9), 100804; preprint first submitted 2022.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed journal paper with author preprint
sources.reviewed: Author preprint abstract and journal publication metadata
sources.supports: Evidence that leakage can create overoptimistic ML evaluations.
sources.limits: General ML methodology, not a benchmark of credential detectors.

sources.citation: Timnit Gebru et al. (2021). Datasheets for Datasets. Communications of the ACM; preprint first submitted 2018.
sources.supports: Document dataset motivation, composition, collection and intended uses.
sources.limits: Our data card adapts the framework; it is not a complete datasheet or a data-quality certification.

sources.citation: Margaret Mitchell et al. (2019). Model Cards for Model Reporting. FAT* 2019; preprint first submitted 2018.
sources.supports: Document intended use, evaluation conditions and limitations.
sources.limits: An empty card does not establish model quality or safety.

sources.citation: Git project. git-diff documentation.
sources.supports: Staged changes compare the index with a commit, normally HEAD.
sources.limits: Not proof that our future reader handles partial staging or untrusted repositories correctly.

sources.citation: git2 maintainers. Repository API documentation.
sources.supports: Available Rust interfaces for staged index/object access.
sources.limits: Use of git2 does not by itself guarantee no external behaviour; audit the pinned version and call path.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. Model persistence.
sources.supports: Untrusted pickle/joblib deserialisation can execute code.
sources.limits: Our bounded JSON loader still needs implementation and adversarial tests.

sources.citation: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series. Secrets Management Cheat Sheet.
sources.reviewed: Lifecycle, rotation, revocation and logging guidance
sources.supports: Secret lifecycle handling and avoiding secret exposure in logs.
sources.limits: Our offline-only scope and synthetic-only data policy are project decisions, not an OWASP certification.

sources.citation: GitHub. Secret scanning and supported secret scanning patterns.
sources.supports: Existing hosted scanning; supported-patterns documentation includes AI-detected patterns.
sources.limits: Features and access can change; no superiority, pricing or completeness claim is made.

sources.citation: Gitleaks maintainers. Gitleaks repository and README.
sources.supports: An existing CLI scanner with commit-workflow integration.
sources.limits: Pin version/configuration for any future comparison; documentation is not an independent benchmark.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. Probability calibration.
sources.supports: Probability interpretation requires assessment of calibration.
sources.limits: No source establishes our vote as calibrated; we deliberately label it an uncalibrated score.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. average_precision_score API documentation.
sources.reviewed: AP definition and comparison with trapezoidal integration
sources.supports: Average precision uses recall-increment weights and differs from trapezoidal PR area.
sources.limits: Does not prescribe our top-k policy or establish project performance.

sources.citation: Git project. gitrepository-layout documentation.
sources.reviewed: Repository structure, Git files, common directories, objects/alternates and repository-format description
sources.supports: Git supports multiple metadata and object-storage layouts.
sources.limits: Veil Guard's refusal policy is narrower and project-specific; Git compatibility does not establish confinement.

sources.citation: libgit2 maintainers. git_repository_open_ext reference and repository implementation, v1.9.7.
sources.type: Official technical documentation and primary source code
sources.reviewed: Explicit open flags; pinned crate source for config loading and environment-dependent object/index paths. Upstream tag corroborated through GitHub API.
sources.supports: Explicit open flags control discovery/environment use; the implementation distinguishes normal versus environment-driven opening.
sources.limits: Library opening can read standard global/system config; the project's preflight and local-config attachment are not a filesystem sandbox.

sources.citation: GitHub. Workflow syntax and GitHub-hosted runners reference.
sources.reviewed: Push/pull-request workflow configuration, permissions, matrix/timeout controls and supported runner labels
sources.supports: Official workflow configuration and hosted-runner labels used by the acceptance pipeline.
sources.limits: A defined workflow or available runner is not a passing CI result; verify the per-commit run.

sources.citation: Astral. uv project guide and locking/syncing documentation.
sources.reviewed: Project manifest/environment structure; locked mode and lockfile consistency checks
sources.supports: Using a uv project and committed lockfile; locked mode refuses automatic lock updates.
sources.limits: A dependency lock does not pin the Python interpreter, prove offline execution or validate numerical parity.

sources.citation: Git project. git-init, Git environment variables and Pro Git: Git Objects.
sources.reviewed: Explicit empty templates, object format and initial branch; configuration/environment overrides; SHA-1 blob header and content hashing
sources.supports: Controls used to initialise isolated authored fixture repositories and verify their staged blob identities.
sources.limits: These documented mechanisms do not prove an operating-system sandbox, validate corpus labels or measure scanner recall.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. LogisticRegression and precision/recall metric API documentation, 1.9.1.
sources.reviewed: LogisticRegression parameters and score outputs; AP threshold weighting and distinction from trapezoidal PR area
sources.supports: API choices for the prespecified logistic baseline and correctly named average precision metric.
sources.limits: Library documentation does not validate this corpus, prescribe the grids or establish project performance.
